KWCH describes the plant as near Conway Springs. The state air permit notice puts the site about five miles southwest of Conway Springs. The mail town is Conway Springs, zip 67031. records.researcher_notes: I compared the sources for this unit. The EIA table for August 2026 lists plant 6064, generator CT4, a natural gas combustion turbine that started in 2006, with nameplate 104 MW and summer and winter capability of 72 MW. The EIA annual survey file for 2024 shows the same three numbers. The Board of Public Utilities testimony from a 2023 rate hearing, by its executive director of electric production, calls CT4 the newest 75 MW oil and gas unit. That testimony does not say whether 75 MW is nameplate, net or summer. It also calls the coal unit 245 Net MW while EIA lists that unit at 261 MW nameplate and 243 MW net, so the testimony appears to use net or operating figures. A 75 MW figure sits close to the 72 MW EIA net rating and well below the 104 MW nameplate, which fits that pattern. A third source, a federal air-data map site, lists a generator 4 at 94 MW, which is probably an older EIA entry and does not match any current rating. I searched for a Board resource plan, annual report, rate filing, Kansas air permit and Southwest Power Pool document that gives the turbine model or a nameplate rating. The Kansas air permit pages did not open and no other document gave a turbine model or a different nameplate. The testimony PDF is gone from the Board's site, but a saved copy from January 2025 still has the 75 MW sentence. I read the EIA annual 2024 file from a local copy; the verifier could not read the zip file.

records.recommendation: Clear the start year of 2031 unless a source for it turns up, or leave it and ask the plant's researcher where it came from. Keep capacity at 720 MW and the owner as Evergy Inc.
records.researcher_notes: GEM shows start year 2031 for unit 1. No document I could read gives a start year for Crooked Creek. The air permit application, the draft permit and the public notice give none. Evergy's 2026 plan update puts its 710 MW combined cycle block for 2031 at Buchanan Bluffs in Missouri, and the Kansas Central petition of September 1, 2026 for prior approval names Buchanan Bluffs and not Crooked Creek. The 2031 year looks carried over from an older Evergy plan placeholder. The other facts check out. The application and draft permit describe one combined cycle block with a Mitsubishi M501JAC turbine, about 720 MW gross and about 705 MW net, so GEM's 720 MW matches the gross figure. The applicant is named as Evergy, Inc, which matches the GEM owner. The saved copy of the draft permit is at https://web.archive.org/web/20260428011600/https://www.kdhe.ks.gov/DocumentCenter/View/58546 and the saved copy of the application is at https://web.archive.org/web/20260428011601/https://www.kdhe.ks.gov/DocumentCenter/View/58616. records.recommendation: No edit. Baird decided on October 23, 2026 that the three 33 MW turbines are one 99 MW unit, as GEM has it now, because together they pass the 50 MW bar on one grid connection.
records.researcher_notes: Unit 2 at Clifton is in GEM as one 99 MW unit made of three 33 MW Solar Turbines Titan 350 turbines, in pre-construction, starting in 2028, replacing unit 1, a Westinghouse 501 turbine from 1974. Sunflower Electric's fact sheet of July 2026 at https://sunflower-epc.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/260708_GEN_CliftonFactSheet_QFT_cf_jw_cf.pdf says it plans three 33 MW Titan 350 turbine generators, with construction beginning in September 2026 and commercial operation in summer 2028. A news report at https://www.ncktoday.com/local/sunflower-electric-power-corp-shares-details-clifton-power-plant-replacement-project repeats those facts. The Southwest Power Pool list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows one request, GEN-2026-GR1, a replacement of 97.844 MW at the Clifton substation owned by Sunflower, with cessation of the old unit on 2/15/2028, commercial operation 6/1/2028, a special study status and a request received on 9/9/2026. The three turbines together are above the bar, so one 99 MW set fits. A standard gas turbine is normally one unit each, and 33 MW is under the bar. The reviewer should pick the arrangement. The grid list figure of 97.844 MW is close to the 99 MW total.

records.recommendation: Decide whether the 721 MW gas request at Jeffrey is the same project as GEM's unit 2, timepoint 2, a 720 MW steam unit announced for 2035, or a new combined cycle block that needs its own unit. I lean toward a separate new block.
records.researcher_notes: The Southwest Power Pool list at https://opsportal.spp.org/Studies/GIActive shows GEN-2024-249 in Pottawatomie County, 721.2 MW of gas with a nameplate of 737.1 MW, at the Jeffrey Energy Center 345 kV substation, owned by Evergy, request received 3/1/2025, in service 1/1/2031 and commercial operation 1/1/2032, still in the cluster study. GEM has Jeffrey unit 2, timepoint 2, as a 720 MW steam turbine, announced, starting in 2035. The nameplate of 737.1 MW is the same as the combined cycle blocks at Viola, request ERAS-2025-008, and at McNew, request ERAS-2025-006. That suggests a new combined cycle block and not a steam unit. The dates also differ, 2031 or 2032 against 2035. No Evergy plan, filing or press release names this request, so no owner statement settles it. I did not add it as a new unit because it may be the unit GEM already has.
